BiblicalUsage: mashshâʼôwn is dissimulation, deceit that covers hatred, and it occurs once, in Proverbs 26:26. There hatred covered by deceit will have its wickedness shown before the whole congregation. The word is the mask that will not hold.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashshâʼôwn shows me that hatred hidden by deceit is still hatred, and that it will be shown before the whole congregation.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
